session_covered: US and European sessions of Thursday 8 October
intro: Covers the US session of Thursday 8 October. The AFR's own column was not accessible; figures come from Trading Economics (CFD-based), Yahoo Finance, Business Recorder and Market Index, and are marked "not available" where they could not be verified.
footnotes: Nasdaq and Dow closes could not be verified (Nasdaq was down roughly 1.4–1.6% intraday late in the session; prior closes 27,538.69 and 51,179.87). S&P 500, yield, AUD, Brent, gold and VIX are Trading Economics CFD-based values; Yahoo Finance intraday showed S&P 500 -0.61% and the 10-year change at -5 bp. VIX % change calculated from the quoted 0.76-pt rise. Iron ore is the 7 October print, the latest available.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures: not available. One quote showed Dec futures +0.28% at 8,746.5, but it was undated and contradicts the risk-off overnight tone, so it is excluded. The prior ASX 200 close was 8,664.30, down 0.77% (a second straight fall). With US equities lower and Brent and yields higher, the tone points to a soft open, but no verified futures figure is available to size it.

what_moved: Tech led US equities lower after an FT report that OpenAI's annualised revenue is about US$50bn, versus US$70bn previously estimated, reviving concerns about AI spending. Nvidia fell about 3% and several chip names fell 4–8%. Eight of 11 S&P 500 sectors fell, led by technology and health care, while energy and consumer staples gained (sector percentages not available). Brent rose above US$104/bbl on Gulf tanker attacks, then eased after President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterms. The 10-year yield touched 5.35%, a 24-year high, before closing lower.

news.headline: OpenAI revenue report hits the AI trade.
news.summary: The FT report put annualised revenue near US$50bn versus US$70bn expected, pressuring chipmakers and AI-linked names.

news.headline: Oil jumps on Gulf shipping attacks, then eases.
news.summary: Brent rose about 4% to US$104.31/bbl; Gulf of Mexico output curbs from a tropical storm added to supply worries.

news.headline: Fed minutes keep a hike on the table.
news.summary: Most officials expect another increase this year, and Governor Waller said more hikes will likely be needed. The 10-year yield ended at 5.23%.

news.headline: US jobless claims fall to 197,000.
news.summary: This was below the 200,000 forecast, pointing to low layoffs.

news.headline: ASX 200 slips to 8,664.30.
news.summary: The index fell 0.77%, with the major banks down about 1.5%, BHP down 2.0% and Rio Tinto down 2.9%.

news.headline: Tech debt-issuance worries.
news.summary: Reports that Broadcom is lining up US$50bn of financing for OpenAI fed concern about heavy borrowing to fund AI buildouts.

news.headline: PepsiCo cuts annual core profit forecast.
news.summary: Shares nonetheless rose 2.1% after a third-quarter beat.

coming_up: US big-bank earnings, including JPMorgan, are due next week (exact date not confirmed).
